correctness.rationale: Ardila's local edge rule is sufficient to reconstruct the graph. Duplicating the current singleton produces a two-copy word. A swap not involving the singleton changes at most one copy inversion, a singleton swap at most two, and a singleton-transfer changes none. The total reversal needs \(2\(n(\(n-1\))\)\) copy inversions. If t labels are never singletons, their pairs force at least \(2t(t-1)\) ordinary swaps; if \(r=n-t\) labels are visited by the singleton and r>=2, the closed singleton-label walk needs at least r transfers. These bounds give length at least \(n^2-1\) for \(n\ge3\), and the explicit block-selection path uses exactly \(n(\(n-1\))\) swaps and \(n-1\) transfers. The \(n=2\) exception is checked separately.

value.rationale: The endpoint pair is canonical: reversal is an explicit symmetry highlighted in the foundational paper. Determining its exact geodesic length yields a quadratic lower bound on the one-skeleton diameter of the natural \((2n-2)\)-dimensional bipermutahedron family. The proof identifies a structural tradeoff between two-copy inversions and singleton transfers, so the result is not a routine finite recomputation or arbitrary parameter slice.
